description:
Sakan proposes the lava caves of the Arabian Peninsula as training grounds for building permanent bases

inside lunar and Martian caves. It presents the idea on an interactive Arabic and English website that brings

the story, the data and the scoring method together in one place.
summary: Sakan is a live, bilingual website that proposes the basalt lava tubes of Arabia's lava fields as new training sites for future cave bases on the Moon and Mars. Scientists see lava caves as some of the safest places to live beyond Earth, because a rock roof blocks cosmic radiation and keeps temperatures steady while the surface swings by hundreds of degrees. Crews will need realistic caves to practice in before they go, and today's analog sites are few and much wetter than the Moon or Mars. Sakan pulls a full year of NASA POWER data over four surveyed Arabian caves and compares them with the sites NASA and ESA use now. The Arabian caves come out far drier, with bigger day-night ground temperature swings. The site ranks the caves for four kinds of tests, from exploration robots to spacesuit walks, and shows the ranking holds when the weights change. It builds a printable training-mission plan for any cave and date, and lets anyone score any place on Earth with the same rules. Sakan turns open NASA data into a tool that space agencies, students and other teams can use and repeat for their own lava fields.
details:
Sakan is a live, bilingual (English and Arabic) website that turns NASA open data into a practical answer to one question: where on Earth can crews train for the cave bases that may one day shelter people on the Moon and Mars?

What it does

The site focuses on four surveyed basalt lava tubes in the lava fields (harrats) of the Arabian Peninsula: Umm Jirsan in Harrat Khaybar, Ghar Al Hibashi in Harrat Nawasif, Kahf Al Shuwaymis in Harrat Ithnayn and Ghostly Cave in Harrat Kishb. Each time the page opens, it requests a full year of daily NASA POWER data above every cave and above two analog sites in use today, Lava Beds in California (NASA) and Lanzarote in Spain (ESA). It then compares rainfall and the day-night swing in ground temperature. The Arabian caves come out far drier and with much larger swings, which brings them closer to the Moon and Mars.

Main features

A live ranking scores the caves for four kinds of tests (general, exploration robots, habitats in the cave, and suits on the surface), with every rule shown on the page. A stability test recalculates the ranking 2,000 times with random changes to the weights, and the top cave stays first in about 99.8% of runs. A mission planner builds a printable training plan for any cave, test and date, using that month's NASA temperatures, local sunrise and sunset, and the sun's position at the Mare Tranquillitatis pit and at Arsia Mons at the same moment. A "check any place" tool lets anyone click a point on Earth and get a climate score from live NASA data with the same rules. Further sections explain radiation shielding, compare tube sizes on Earth, Mars and the Moon to scale, and show what our caves can and cannot stand in for at a south-pole base versus a lava-cave base. All the data can be downloaded as CSV.

Impact

Space agencies gain new, well-documented training sites. More than six million school students in Saudi Arabia alone can explore Moon and Mars science in Arabic with real data. The lava fields gain scientific and tourism value, and any team in the world can repeat the method for its own lava fields.

How we built it

HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript in a single file with no server, Leaflet for the maps, NASA GIBS, Moon Trek and Mars Trek tiles, the NASA POWER API, and in-browser astronomy for the Moon and Mars clocks based on NASA's Mars24 algorithm. The 30-second demo is drawn frame by frame in code.

Limitations

NASA POWER cells are about 50 km wide, so values describe the region rather than the cave mouth. The access score is our own estimate, and no one has yet measured conditions inside lunar or Martian caves. The site states these limits where they apply.
